items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: she even was my teaching assistant while she was a senior

ctx.x: To wrap up, I know you’ve got to be very proud that you’ve got some upcoming generations of musicians in our family.

My daughter chose to go into music, but she chose to go into music at the last minute. When she was getting ready to graduate from high school, she made the decision the last year, because she said she thought I wouldn’t be happy with her if she didn’t do all the same things that I did. I convinced her that was not the case at all. So she took up violin. But when she graduated from college – she was the first string player to graduate from the jazz program [at Indiana University] – when she graduated from…

and was doing very, very well in that thing. There was no music at all. She wasn’t doing any music at all. She was simply doing this. And I thought it [was] kind of ironic, because when they had the bi[centennial] – the centennial, or whatever the sesqui[centennial] – whatever it was . . .
